title: Late Breaking Results: Coulomb Force-Based Routability-Driven Placement Considering Global and Local Congestion
problem: VLSI placement engines that ignore layout congestion produce poor solutions with routing failures. The challenge is optimizing cell placement while mitigating both global and local routing congestion.
motivation: Placement quality directly determines routability; poor congestion-aware placement decisions lead to unresolvable routing failures.
method: The framework uses a routing path-based cell padding strategy for local congestion mitigation. It constructs a routability-aware placement model employing virtual Coulomb forces (electrostatic repulsion) to eliminate global congestion by pushing cells apart based on congestion density.
key_novelty: Using virtual Coulomb forces as a physics-inspired mechanism to directly optimize placement for simultaneous global and local routing congestion mitigation.
contributions: Routing path-based cell padding strategy for local congestion mitigation
Routability-aware placement model using virtual Coulomb forces for global congestion elimination
Achieves best routability with shortest runtime versus RePlAce and Innovus on industrial benchmarks
